tagline: Along the Wabash, past a replica fort a mile astray.
intro: The road sets out from Ross Hills County Park, west of West Lafayette, and keeps to the Wabash on South River Road and North River Road, the old State Road 43, as far as I-65 near Battle Ground. Since 2016 it has gone by the Wabash River Scenic Byway, the better to celebrate the river.

In 1717 the French built Fort Ouiatenon here as a trading post among the Wea, the first fortified European settlement in what is now Indiana. Near the I-65 end, Prophetstown State Park recalls the village Tecumseh and his brother Tenskwatawa founded in 1808.

moments.title: Ross Hills County Park
moments.text: The byway begins at 168 acres of trails and a deck overlook, part of nearly four contiguous miles of habitat along the Wabash.

moments.title: Fort Ouiatenon Historic Park
moments.text: In 1930 a local doctor built a replica blockhouse here of horizontal, British-style logs, about a mile east of where the vertical-log French fort actually stood.

moments.title: Tecumseh Trails Park
moments.text: On North River Road, across from the Indiana Veterans' Home, a small county park with a shelter house overlooks the Wabash.
